extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and readers interested in American poetry and aesthetic theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and evaluative standards for composing and judging poetry—especially 'democratic' or national poetry—emphasizing sincerity, maturity, moral scope, and context over mere polish or fashionable forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art is one (inclusive view of art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is one, is not partial, but includes all times and forms and sorts--is not exclusively aristocratic or democratic, or oriental or occidental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art should not be segregated by class, nation, or period; the evaluator/creator should recognize a single, inclusive conception of Art that spans styles and cultures. Whitman uses the symbol of a font that 'rejects nothing' to emphasize openness to diverse sources and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic art arises from democratic development
rubrics_metrics.description: Democratic art results of democratic development, from tinge, true nationality, belief, in the one setting up from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic democratic poetry must grow organically from the nation's democratic life and convictions (an 'autochthonic, interior, constitutional' change), not be merely an imitation of aristocratic models; national character and belief should infuse the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize central purpose over style and polish
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson of Nature undoubted is, to proceed with single purpose toward the result necessitated, and for which the time has arrived, utterly regardless of the outputs of shape, appearance or criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form, technique, and rhetorical ornament should not be allowed to master the work; style is secondary and acceptable only so far as it serves the central, necessary expression or purpose of the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity as a central, heroic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: By sincerity itself, becomes heroic; the heart of him is of the true Prophet cast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine sincerity in voice and conviction is a defining artistic virtue—more valuable than transcendent intellect or technical virtuosity—and can elevate modest talent to heroic stature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature, accreted atmosphere as the final proof of greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: The final proof of song or personality is a sort of matured, accreted, superb, evoluted, almost divine, impalpable diffuseness and atmosphere or invisible magnetism, dissolving and embracing all--and not any special achievement of passion, pride, metrical form, epigram, plot, thought, or what is call'd beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The highest poetic achievement is an ineffable, integrated aura produced by long development—an accumulated 'atmosphere'—rather than an isolated technical feat or dazzling device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of old age and long experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps, indeed, the rarest and most blessed quality of transcendent noble poetry... is, (I would suggest,) from sane, completed, vital, capable old age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems (and poets) often reach their fullest, most authoritative expression late in life; evaluators should recognize maturity and longevity as key contributors to depth and greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual evaluation: weigh age, politics, aim, and times
rubrics_metrics.description: No great poem or other literary or artistic work of any scope... can be essentially consider'd without weighing first the age, politics (or want of politics) and aim, visible forms, unseen soul, and current times, out of the midst of which it rises and is formulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical judgment must account for historical, political, social, and personal context of a work's creation—its 'background' and the conditions that produced it—when assessing significance or success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry should aspire to lofty moral, spiritual, and heroic illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the production (and on the most copious scale) of loftiest moral, spiritual and heroic personal illustrations--a great native Literature headed with a Poetry stronger and sweeter than any yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national or 'kosmic' significance, poetry should aim to produce exemplary moral/spiritual figures or demonstrations in life and art—works that embody high ethical and heroic worth, not merely technical cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt aesthetics to new world / democratic conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For New World service our ideas of beauty (inherited from the Greeks, and so on to Shakspere--_query_--perverted from them?) need to be radically changed, and made anew for to-day's purposes and finer standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators should not slavishly inherit classical or Old World standards; they should reformulate notions of beauty appropriate to contemporary democratic societies and purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over provenance: value good material regardless of source
rubrics_metrics.description: The font is about the same forever. Democratic art results of democratic development... 'I never bother myself what road the folks come--I only want good wheat and rye.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of material/content matters more than the social origin or pedigree of its creator; inclusivity of sources is acceptable so long as the result is 'good' in substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of common critical expectations (humor, polish, plot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ruskin... charges... my poems have no humor. A profound German critic complains that... there is about my verse a certain coldness, severity, absence of spice, polish, or of consecutive meaning and plot. E.C. Stedman finds... fault... because while celebrating the common people en masse I do not allow enough heroism and moral merit... to the choicer classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Whitman contests some of these expectations, practitioners should know that critics often value humor, warmth, polish, narrative coherence, and manifest heroism in certain social registers—these are recurring standards of appraisal one may encounter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry needs great readers/audience to achieve heroic status
rubrics_metrics.description: To have great heroic poetry we need great readers--a heroic appetite and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The possibility of certain poetic forms or greatness depends on an audience's capacity and appetite; creators should consider cultural reception and, where possible, cultivate readership enabling the work's aims.
